paragraph_html: Stream entry’s greatest prize is a “release date”: AN 3.88 allows at most seven more lives before final awakening. There is actually quite a lot of modern academic evidence for rebirth. But who’s going around getting reborn if no permanent self exists? Buddhists don’t imagine any permanent self-essence/soul moving between bodies. What continues is a chain of causes with no traveler riding along, often called a mind-stream: craving and clinging condition becoming, and becoming becomes birth. More like a driverless car. The later Buddhist philosopher Milindapañha compared rebirth to one lamp being used to lighting another.

candidates.n2_rebirth_bj: Rather, rebirth is seen as a causal process: there is a continuity (often called a “mind-stream”), but there is not a “thing” that’s moving from one life to the next. Craving and clinging lead to becoming, and becoming leads to birth.
candidates.n2_rebirth_bk: Instead, rebirth is the causal continuation of one life into the next, sometimes referred to as the mind-stream. In brief, craving and clinging lead to becoming, which leads to birth.
candidates.n2_rebirth_mine: Craving and clinging keep “becoming” going, and becoming is what leads to the next birth, so what carries on is a chain of causes (some call it a mind-stream) with nobody riding along inside it.
